bloques.html: Instructions: Read each question carefully. For multiple-choice questions, mark the letter of the correct answer with an ✗. Write complete sentences when there are lines. We start with Listening: an adult will read some instructions aloud twice.

bloques.html:
Read the poem and answer questions 6 to 9.

Rain on the Roof

The rain taps on the tin roof like a thousand tiny drums,
It hums a sleepy lullaby until the morning comes.
The street becomes a river, the garden is a lake,
The old dog sighs beside the fire and dreams of summer steak.

The clouds are grey wool blankets pulled across the sky,
The wind is a wild horse that gallops, whistling, by.
I press my nose against the glass and watch the puddles grow,
And count the silver ribbons where the gutters overflow.

Tomorrow there'll be sunshine and the sky will be bright blue,
But tonight the rain is music, and I'm glad I'm listening too.
"The rain taps on the tin roof like a thousand tiny drums" is an example of... (1 pt)

alternativas.html: The clouds are made of wool.
The clouds are thick and cover the whole sky, like a blanket.
Someone hung blankets outside to dry.

bloques.html: "The clouds are grey wool blankets pulled across the sky." What does the poet mean? (1 pt)

pauta.respuesta: B) The clouds are thick and cover the whole sky, like a blanket

bloques.html: Which pair of words rhymes in the poem? (1 pt)
How does the speaker of the poem feel about the rain? (1 pt)

pauta.respuesta: C) Calm and happy ("the rain is music, and I'm glad")
pauta.oa: RL.5.2 — tono y actitud del hablante

Read the story and answer questions 10 to 12.

The Spelling Bee

"I'm not going," said Nico, pushing his cereal around the bowl. "I'll forget every word."

His sister Paula didn't look up from her book. "You knew all of them last night."

"That was in the kitchen. Tomorrow it's on a stage, with lights, and everyone staring."

Paula closed her book. "Do you remember when I learned to ride my bike?"

"You fell about a hundred times."

"Ninety-two," she said. "I counted. And then I didn't fall anymore."

Nico frowned. "Spelling isn't riding a bike."

"No," said Paula. "It's easier. If you fall, you just say the next letter."

Nico was quiet for a while. Then he picked up his spoon, finished his cereal, and went to find his list of words.

The next day he came third. He misspelled "necessary". He didn't mind very much.

alternativas.html: He is afraid of making mistakes in front of people.
Paula told him not to go.

bloques.html: Why doesn't Nico want to go to the spelling bee? (1 pt)

pauta.respuesta: B) He is afraid of making mistakes in front of people
pauta.oa: RL.5.1 — inferencia apoyada en el texto

alternativas.html: To show Nico that she is better than him

Because she wants to go for a ride

bloques.html: Why does Paula tell the story about her bike? (1 pt)

pauta.respuesta: B) To show that falling, or making mistakes, is part of learning

alternativas.html: It is better to stay home than to fail.

Spelling is harder than riding a bike.

bloques.html: Which sentence best states the theme of the story? (1 pt)

pauta.respuesta: C) Being brave means trying even when you might make a mistake

Talk with the adult: explain how to do something step by step and tell a story. (8 pts)

pauta.oa: OA10-13 / Flyers Speaking — proceso y narración

pautaHtml:
Guion de Listening (leer dos veces, en voz alta)

Lee a ritmo normal, marcando las palabras de secuencia (first, second, third, finally). Pausa de 30 segundos entre lecturas.

How to Make a Paper Kite

Today I'm going to teach you how to make a simple kite. You need four things: a large sheet of thin paper, two thin wooden sticks, a roll of string, and tape.

First, lay the paper flat on a table. Place one stick straight down the middle, from top to bottom. Place the second stick across it, about one third of the way down from the top, so the two sticks make a cross. Tape the sticks to the paper where they meet.

Second, fold the edges of the paper over the ends of the sticks and tape them down. This keeps the kite from tearing in the wind.

Third, tie one end of the string to the point where the sticks cross. Make sure the knot is tight. This is the most important step: if the knot slips, your kite will fly away without you.

Finally, cut a strip of paper about one meter long and tape it to the bottom of the kite. This is the tail. A kite without a tail spins and crashes.

Now wait for a windy day, hold the string, run, and let go!

Guion de Speaking (4-5 minutos)

Solo en inglés. No corrijas durante la conversación; anota y califica al final.

  1. Warm-up (30 s, no se califica): "Hi! Is it raining today? Do you like rainy days?"
  2. Process (2 min): "Explain to me, step by step, how to play your favorite game (a board game, a playground game or a video game). What do you need, how do you start, and how do you win?" Apoyo: "What happens next?" / "What is the last step?"
  3. Story (2 min): "Tell me about a time you were nervous about something, like Nico in the story. What happened at the beginning, in the middle and at the end?" Apoyo: "How did you feel?" / "What did you do?" / "How did it end?"
  4. Cierre: "Thank you, that's all."

Rúbricas

Escritura (ítem 17) — 1 punto por criterio cumplido:

Criterio 1 pt si...
Contenido Dos personajes, uno nervioso y otro que ayuda; se entiende la situación; 4-6 líneas
Organización Cada intervención en una línea nueva; se sabe quién habla (said Ana, asked Tomás...)
Puntuación del diálogo Comillas al inicio y fin de lo dicho, coma o punto dentro de las comillas, mayúscula al comenzar la cita; máximo 1 error
Apóstrofes Al menos una contracción y un posesivo bien escritos (I'm, don't, Ana's)
Ortografía y gramática Oraciones completas; máximo 2 errores de ortografía o gramática

Speaking (ítem 18) — cada criterio 0, 1 o 2 puntos:

Criterio 2 pts 1 pt 0 pts
Contenido Explica el juego completo (materiales, inicio, cómo se gana) y cuenta la historia con sus tres partes y cómo se sintió Faltan pasos del juego o la historia es incompleta Respuestas mínimas o no responde
Organización Pasos y hechos en orden con conectores (first, then, after that, finally, because) Orden confuso o sin conectores Sin estructura
Vocabulario Variado y preciso; usa palabras de sentimiento (nervous, scared, relieved, proud) Repite palabras básicas o cambia a español en 1-2 palabras Muy limitado; mezcla español con frecuencia
Corrección Tiempos verbales y concordancia correctos casi siempre (máximo 2 errores) Varios errores que no impiden entender Errores constantes que dificultan entender

Qué mira este instrumento

Fase B. Comprensión auditiva de un texto instructivo con inferencia (1-5); lectura de un poema con símil, metáfora, rima y actitud del hablante (6-9), al nivel CCSS RL.5.4; lectura de un cuento con diálogo para inferir motivaciones y tema (10-12); prefijos y sinónimos (13-14); puntuación de enumeraciones, apóstrofes y comillas (15-16); escritura de un diálogo (17); speaking de proceso y narración (18).

Señales: si falla 6-7, no distingue aún el lenguaje literal del figurado: hay que leer poesía en voz alta y preguntar "¿es verdad literalmente?". Si falla 12, identifica hechos pero no extrae el mensaje; preguntar "¿qué aprendió el personaje?" después de cada cuento. Si 15-16 están mal pero el speaking es bueno, es convención escrita pura (comillas y apóstrofes), muy típica de bilingües no escolarizados en inglés, y se corrige rápido con práctica de copia. Si en 17 pierde "puntuación del diálogo" y "apóstrofes" a la vez, prioriza eso la semana siguiente.

Si le fue mal

  • Lenguaje figurado: cazar símiles y metáforas en canciones en inglés que le gusten (una por día) y explicar qué significan de verdad.
  • Tema: después de cada cuento o película, pedirle que termine la frase "The story teaches that...".
  • Comillas y apóstrofes: copiar 5 líneas de diálogo de un libro en inglés fijándose en la puntuación; luego dictarle 3 líneas.
  • Prefijos y sufijos: hacer una tabla de la casa con un-, re-, dis-, -ful, -less y agregar palabras nuevas durante la semana.
  • Listening de instrucciones: que siga en inglés una receta simple leída por un adulto (hacer un sándwich, una limonada) sin ver el texto.
